artworks.title: Portrait of Christiane Henriette Koch as Pelopia
artworks.description: Johann Friedrich Bause's Metropolitan Museum print shows the actress Christiane Henriette Koch costumed as Pelopia — Thyestes' daughter and mother of Aegisthus in the Atreid horror. Eighteenth-century stage culture kept the Sicyonian tragedy of the sword and the unrecognized incest alive as a role for leading ladies.

popCulture.title: Bibliotheca
popCulture.creator: Apollodorus
popCulture.description: Apollodorus tells how Thyestes begets Aegisthus on his own daughter Pelopia — the night at Sicyon, the stolen sword, and the infant who will kill Atreus.

popCulture.title: Pelopia
popCulture.description: Daughter of Thyestes, mother of Aegisthus — the woman whose recognition of the sword seals Atreus' doom.

popCulture.title: Aegisthus
popCulture.description: Pelopia's son by Thyestes — the usurper lover of Clytemnestra whose birth is the Atreid curse made flesh.

popCulture.title: Thyestes
popCulture.description: Pelopia's father — and, in the darkest strand, the father of her child Aegisthus — the banquet and the incest as twin horrors of the house.
